messages:
Priya (Billing): Heads-up: Partner invoices for Acme Integrations (acct: acme-int) in today's batch show wrong totals. Looks like partner_discount applied twice on line items for three customers. Example invoice shows:

Invoice INV-AC-20260402-003
compute: 300.00
partner_discount: -150.00
partner_discount: -150.00  # duplicate
net_due: 0.00  # should be 150.00

Preview CSV: s3://billing-exports/prod/2026-04-02/acme-int-batch.csv
Can FinOps/Eng take a look?

Oscar (FinOps): That net_due=0.00 is bad. Can you attach the invoice generation run id and the pricing rule set id used? Also any recent changes to discount application logic?

Priya (Billing): Run id batch-run-20260402-22. pricing_rule_set=partner-v2. No changes in billing code this week. Note: payments team deployed pricing-rule resolver last night (2026-04-02T01:05 UTC).

Nina (Eng): Assigning to me. Quick grep of template code shows discount application loop:
```
for rule in applicable_rules:
  if rule.type == 'partner_discount':
    total -= apply_discount(rule, line)
```
I also see a recent PR that reworked rule merging; suspect applicable_rules contains duplicate entries for partner-v2 if both rule_id and alias match. Reproducing locally with acme fixtures.

billing-bot: Detected anomaly: duplicate_discount_lines=3 tenants=[acme-01, acme-02, acme-03] run=batch-run-20260402-22

Leo (Payments): We did deploy a resolver that merges rules from Pricing DB and a cached PartnerRules table to improve failover. If both sources contain partner-v2, the merge currently keeps both copies. I'll rollback the resolver change to stop further bad invoices and we can hotfix merging logic.

Support (Emma): Acme support pinged via email, upset about net due 0 and then being charged unexpectedly later. They want corrected invoices and an explanation. I suggested temporary credit while we fix.

Oscar (FinOps): Plan: 1) Pause outgoing sends for batch-run-20260402-22 (Priya) 2) Roll back resolver (Leo) 3) Fix merge logic to dedupe rules by canonical_id or rule_hash (Nina) 4) Recompute invoices for affected tenants and run reconciliation diff report (billing-reconciliation/2026-04-02/partner-acme-diff). 5) Send corrected invoices and reverse any incorrect Stripe captures.

Priya (Billing): Pause applied for run=batch-run-20260402-22. Also opened Stripe investigation for pre-captured payment: pi_3Lk...abc - holding capture.

Nina (Eng): Root cause found: when partner rules are present in both Pricing DB and PartnerRules cache, merge produced two range entries with same canonical_id but different source flags, so dedupe failed. Hotfix: dedupe by canonical_id and prefer Pricing DB source for priority. Adding unit test and integration test against partner fixtures. ETA ~2 hours to deploy to prod after CI.

Leo (Payments): Rolled back resolver to previous release at 1721102502. No new bad invoices since rollback.

billing-bot: Action: pause_auto_send for run=batch-run-20260402-22 by Priya at 1721102510

Oscar (FinOps): After reissue we'll run automated checks: for each invoice verify sum(line_items) + sum(discounts) == gross_total and discount_count <= 1 for partner_discount per invoice. Also audit partner_rules table for duplicates across data sources.

Priya (Billing): I'll notify Acme with this message: "We're fixing a duplicate discount application that incorrectly zeroed some invoices in today's batch. We've paused sends, will reissue corrected invoices and reverse any erroneous captures. Sorry for the disruption." Replying to customer now.

Nina (Eng): Hotfix merged to main and deployed to prod at 1721102568. Running reissue in staging now; if green I'll queue prod reissue. Posting results in this thread.

Priya (Billing): Thanks team. Leaving thread open until reissue + reconciliation pass complete.
